label: th:Diff
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Sharp diffusivity asymptotics

title: Remark
body_md: The explicit form of $d^{\lim}$ has noteworthy features. First, after the adequate identification of parameters (see~\eqref{e:ASEPFormalSBE}), it coincides not only with the prefactor appearing in the mode-coupling computations of~\cite{vBKS}, but also with the diffusivity prefactor obtained for the two-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation in~\cite{CMT25}. More strikingly, the $\lambda^{4/3}$ proportionality is shared by one-dimensional models in the KPZ universality class, even though their diffusivity grows as $t^{1/3}$ rather than logarithmically. In addition, the symmetric jump rates enter the leading prefactor only through the transverse component $D_0[\mathfrak{f},\mathfrak{f}]$; in particular it is independent of $D_0[\mathfrak{e},\mathfrak{e}]$. The scaling argument of~\cite[Remark~1.2]{CMT25} draws a connection between this independence and the powers $\lambda^{4/3}$ and $D_0[\mathfrak{f},\mathfrak{f}]^{-1/3}$.
head: environment

label: th:CLT2ndClass
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Central limit theorem for the second class particle

title: Remark
body_md: Theorem~\ref{th:CLT2ndClass} identifies the scaling limit of the second-class particle for one time marginal. It would be interesting to investigate joint convergence for several time marginals, or even a functional scaling limit. We stress however that this is an highly nontrivial question: in particular, we are not aware of any scaling limit results beyond one time marginal for the second-class particle in the ASEP in dimension $d \geq 3$.
head: environment

label: th:CLT
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Superdiffusive invariance principle

title: Remark
body_md: Theorem~\ref{th:CLT} exhibits a characteristic feature of systems at their critical dimension. The microscopic fluctuation field must be observed under a logarithmically superdiffusive scaling, whereas the limiting Gaussian process $Y^{\lim}$ is itself invariant under diffusive scaling. Hence, the logarithmic correction disappears after taking the scaling limit. A similar phenomenon occurs for the two-dimensional Stochastic Burgers Equation~\cite{CMT25} and for the diffusion in a critically correlated incompressible random drift~\cite{ABRK24}.

label: rmk:fLSBE
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk:fLSBE}
Formally, ${\mathfrak L}$ can be interpreted as the generator of the SBE
 egin{equ} \label{e:ASEPTrueSBE}
(\partial_t + v \cdot 
abla) \, u =  rac{1}{2} \, 
abla \cdot D_0 
abla u + \sqrt{\varrho(1-\varrho)} \, \mathfrak{w} \cdot 
abla \chi * (\chi * u)^2 + 
abla \cdot  ig(\sqrt{D_0} \, \vec{\, \xi} ig) \, ,
\end{equ}
where the mollifier $\chi$ is given by the ultraviolet Fourier cut-off ${\mathfrak F}^{-1}((2 \pi)^{-1} \1_{|\cdot|_\infty < \pi})$. Compare~\eqref{e:ASEPTrueSBE} to the heuristic equation~\eqref{e:ASEPFormalSBE}: here, we have an additional transport term because we have not yet performed the Galilean transformation, and the non-linearity is regularised via the mollifier $\chi$, which is connected to the choice of the cut-off $\Pi_{p,q} = 2 \pi \hat \chi(p) 	imes 2 \pi \hat \chi(q) 	imes 2 \pi \hat \chi(p+q)$ in~\eqref{e:CutOff}. Heuristically, ${\mathfrak S}$ corresponds to the generator of the diffusive part $ rac{1}{2} \, 
abla \cdot D_0 
abla u + 
abla \cdot \sqrt{D_0} \, \vec{\xi}$, while ${\mathfrak A}_+ + {\mathfrak A}_-$ comes from the non-linearity $\sqrt{\varrho(1-\varrho)} \, \mathfrak{w} \cdot 
abla \chi * (\chi * u^2)$ and ${\mathfrak A}_0$ from the transport term $v \cdot 
abla u$. For a more rigorous statement, we refer to~\cite{CMT25}; we stress however that, although the connection between ${\mathfrak L}$ and the generator of the SBE is enlightening, we do not need this interpretation of ${\mathfrak L}$ in this work (in particular, we do not need the well-posedness of the SPDE~\eqref{e:ASEPTrueSBE}).

abla$ in each chaos variable, which is consistent with Remark~ef{rmk:A0}. In particular, let us stress that ${\mathfrak A}_0$ commutes with every translation invariant operator, such as ${\mathfrak S}$, ${\mathfrak A}_+$, ${\mathfrak A}_-$ or any diagonal operator (cf. the definition just below).

body_md: Compared to other similar estimates that can be found in the literature, the bounds~\eqref{e:KolmogorovM} and~\eqref{e:KolmogorovI} have two key advantages: on the one hand, we can consider functionals $f$ and $g$ with infinite chaos decompositions, provided that we control their exponential decay in $N$ (which we do, for example, in the estimates of Proposition~\ref{p:AnsatzA+ASEP}); on the other hand, we do not need any control on quantities such as $\|\nabla f\|_\infty := \sup_{\eta \in \Omega, \, x \sim y \in \mathbb{Z}^2} |f(\eta^{x,y}) - f(\eta)|$ to control the size of the jumps of $M_\cdot^\tau(f)$ (which we do not have, for example, for the corrector $\mathrm{Cor}_t^{\tau, \mu}(\varphi)$).

title: Remark
body_md: It would be possible to strengthen Proposition~\ref{p:CVfindim} in two ways. First, the convergences~\eqref{e:CVfindimAnnealed} and~\eqref{e:CVfindimQuenched} hold uniformly over the sampling times $t_1, \dots, t_n \geq 0$. Second, if we assume $f$ to be smooth with at most polynomial growth, then the errors with respect to the convergences~\eqref{e:CVfindimAnnealed} and~\eqref{e:CVfindimQuenched} can be bounded by $O(\log_{*}(\tau)^{-1/6 + o(1)})$. Indeed, these improvements could be obtained, respectively, from the uniformity in time in the convergence~\eqref{e:CVsemigroupFock} and from the quantitative estimate~\eqref{e:QuantitativeCVsemigroup}. However, since implementing these refinements would require additional work, we prefer to stick to the simpler statement of Proposition~\ref{p:CVfindim}.
